gates.text: Voice and humor fit the business evidence, audience, approved brand style, market and destination platform; sensitive topics are not trivialized.

Any current-trend claim has a source URL, date, and source-reported observation tied to the same research record; the deterministic freshness check passes, otherwise the idea is evergreen or labeled unverified.
The post uses an original, useful business-specific idea and does not promise virality, copy protected creator assets, or use engagement bait.

anchors.1: Uses a generic voice or a stereotype about the industry; the audience fit is unclear.
anchors.3: Generally fits the category and audience but could belong to many businesses.
anchors.5: The tone and idea fit this business's approved voice, customer situation, offer and risk level.

anchors.1: Copies the same joke, format or copy across platforms, including a mismatch with platform norms.
anchors.3: Makes some format changes but misses a meaningful audience or policy distinction.
anchors.5: Rewrites the idea natively for each platform and avoids formats or tone that conflict with its current context.

anchors.1: Invents or overstates a trend, or uses one only because it is popular.
anchors.3: Finds a plausible current reference but its audience or business connection is weak.
anchors.5: Uses a recent cited signal only when audience, brand and platform fit are clear; otherwise chooses evergreen content.

anchors.1: A copied meme wrapper with no useful business point.
anchors.3: A recognizable format with a relevant but familiar point.
anchors.5: An original, shareable expression of a specific customer insight that remains useful without the trend.
